title: Builder Signals · 2026-06-21
summary: Follow Builders 今日捕捉到 22 条 X 动态、1 集播客、1 篇博客；本站精选 8 条高信号内容。

featured.title: Guillermo Rauch · Vercel CEO
featured.summaryEn: Vercel CEO Guillermo Rauch shared a provocative take this week: the next hot programming language is markdown. He showed a minimal agent—an `instructions.md` plus markdown files in a `skills/` folder—deployable with a single `vercel` command, calling it the most accessible programming has ever been, and likely will ever be for the generation of software fully defined and controlled by humans. In a second post he argued agents are reviving a wave of healthy software habits: open APIs, documentation (skills), tests…
featured.insightZh: Vercel CEO Guillermo Rauch 这周抛出一个挺有意思的观点：下一个最热门的编程语言是 markdown。他展示了一个极简 agent 的结构——一个 `instructions.md` 加一个 `skills/` 目录里的 markdown 文件，一条 `vercel` 命令就能部署。他说这是编程有史以来最易上手的方式，可能也是人类完全定义和掌控软件这一代里的极致。另一条推文里他进一步论证：agent 正在倒逼一堆健康的软件习惯回归——开放 API、文档（skills）、测试（evals）、Unix（CLI）、支付与商务协议，连 markdown/json/html 这种宽 `Accept` 用法都回来了。在他眼里，万维网最初的愿景正在我们眼前重新成真。

featured.title: Aaron Levie · Box CEO
featured.summaryEn: Box CEO Aaron Levie argues the main variable for agent success is whether you can give the agent the context it needs—and a major factor is creating a shared working area both the human and the agent can understand. This, he says, is why agents using filesystems is such a big deal: it builds a unified system where person and agent can pass data back and forth. Citing the idea that agents need a working set—plans, notes, task lists, policies, drafts, summaries, logs, corrections, decisions—he notes a filesystem-sha…
featured.insightZh: Box CEO Aaron Levie 点出 agent 成功的核心变量：你能不能把 agent 完成工作所需的上下文喂给它——而其中一个关键因素，是能否建立一个人和 agent 都看得懂的共享工作区。这正是「agent 用文件系统」之所以重要的原因：它创造了一个人和 agent 都能在里面传递数据的统一系统。他引用了一段话——agent 需要的是一个工作集：计划、笔记、任务清单、策略、草稿、摘要、日志、纠错、决策等等；对这一层来说，文件系统形态的接口对模型和监管它的人都更易读。结论是：把我们已经会用的系统，以最适合 agent 的方式开放给它，就是 agent 工作的完美原语。

featured.title: Re-engineering the Semiconductor Supply Chain with Intel CEO Lip Bu Tan
featured.summaryEn: Intel CEO Lip Bu Tan breaks down how he's trying to "save Intel" through a VC veteran's lens—crawl, walk, run; simplify products; strengthen the balance sheet; and bet on the return of the CPU in the AI era plus domestic chip manufacturing. Lip Bu Tan is a legendary semiconductor investor (Walden founder), former Cadence CEO, and now Intel CEO. At 66 he took what he calls the hardest job in the industry, when many told him to retire. His most surprising moment: one early morning President Trump asked him to resign over a conflict of interest. He convinced himself "I don't need this job—I do it purely to save Intel," set the personal issue aside, and ultimately won a chance to explain himself. His playbook follows a startup cadence: first crawl—stay humble, listen to customers, and strengthen a balance sheet he bluntly calls "really horrible." He made the US government a major shareholde…
featured.insightZh: Intel CEO 陈立武（Lip Bu Tan）以风投老兵的视角拆解他如何「拯救 Intel」——先「爬、再走、最后跑」，砍产品、强资产负债表，押注 AI 时代 CPU 的回归与本土晶圆制造。 陈立武是传奇半导体投资人（Walden 创始人）、Cadence 前 CEO，现任 Intel CEO。66 岁接下这份「全行业最难的工作」时，很多人劝他退休。他坦言最意外的一幕是某个清晨特朗普总统要他辞职、指其有利益冲突——他说服自己「我不需要这份工作，纯粹是为了救 Intel」，把个人因素放一边后再去想能为公司做什么，最终在一次会面里赢得了机会。 他的打法是典型的创业者节奏：先「爬」——保持谦逊、倾听客户、强化资产负债表（他直言「这资产负债表某种意义上糟透了」），让美国政府成为大股东，老友黄仁勋投的 50 亿美元如今已变成 250 亿。再砍产品线、让所有工程团队直接向他汇报。一个反直觉的判断是 CPU 在 AI 时代正强势回归：「在训练上 CPU 对 GPU 的比例曾是 1:8，现在我看到 1:4，甚至可能 1:1」——他说在强化学习和编排海量 agent 时，CPU 反而更合适。 他还把代工（Foundry）定义为一门「信任生意」——客户要先信你才肯把晶圆订单交给你，所以良率、缺陷密度、周期时间是命脉。展望十年后的赢家，他押注「激光聚焦于一个细分、找对合伙人、并能规模化」的全栈公司，并引用黄仁勋专注 CUDA 做平台、以及 Anthropic / OpenAI 这类初创「以更优雅的方式改变游戏」为范本。他的投资哲学一以贯之：找真正需要解决的瓶颈、找对合伙人、看应用够不够大——「我投的 10 家公司里有 9 家中途改了商业计划，因为市场变了」，所以他要的是一支创业者团队，而非单打独斗的一个人。

items.title: Boris Cherny · Anthropic Claude Code
items.summaryEn: Boris Cherny of Anthropic's Claude Code team highlighted an unusual use of Claude Code: deciphering Linear A, a roughly 3,500-year-old written language from Crete. He shared a link and joked he hopes it holds up in peer review. It's a fun example of pointing a coding agent at humanities and archaeology research, a reminder these tools reach well beyond writing code.
items.insightZh: Anthropic Claude Code 团队的 Boris Cherny 分享了一个 Claude Code 的非典型用法：用它来破译线性文字 A（Linear A）——一种来自克里特岛、距今约 3500 年的古老书写系统。他附了链接并半开玩笑地说「希望这能撑过同行评审」。这是一个把编程 agent 用于人文与考古研究的有趣案例，说明这类工具的应用边界远不止写代码。

items.title: Swyx · Latent Space / AI Engineer
items.summaryEn: Swyx, Latent Space co-host and AI Engineer conference organizer, amplified a striking prediction: Anthropic will IPO at a $2T valuation. The quote-tweet drew nearly 270 likes, reflecting how closely the community is watching frontier-lab valuations climb. Set against his activity at the AI Engineer World's Fair—where his crew is even producing the first-ever physical daily newspaper—it's a useful thermometer for current AI startup and capital fervor.
items.insightZh: Latent Space 联合主播、AI Engineer 大会组织者 Swyx 引用并放大了一条预测：Anthropic 将以 2 万亿美元估值 IPO。这条带评论的转发收获了近 270 个赞，反映出社区对前沿大模型公司估值狂飙的关注度。结合他正在 AI Engineer World's Fair 现场（甚至在做首份实体每日报纸）的背景，这是观察当下 AI 创业与资本热度的一个温度计。

items.title: Garry Tan · Y Combinator CEO
items.summaryEn: Y Combinator president and CEO Garry Tan offered a counterintuitive board tip: for your next board meeting, take the worst thing you're afraid to show your board and make it slide one—then make a big deal of having done it, and turn it into a habit. He notes this only works with good boards. The logic: surfacing bad news front and center builds trust and speeds problem-solving, rather than burying it until the end.
items.insightZh: YC 总裁兼 CEO Garry Tan 给了一条反直觉的董事会建议：下次开董事会，把你最怕拿给董事看的那件最糟糕的事，做成第一页幻灯片——而且大张旗鼓地强调你这么做了，把它变成习惯。他补充说这只有在董事会质量好的前提下才行得通。背后的逻辑是：主动把坏消息摆到最显眼处，反而建立信任、加速解决问题，而不是把问题藏到最后。

items.title: Zara Zhang · Builder / Follow Builders 作者
items.summaryEn: Zara Zhang, author of the Follow Builders project, distilled a sharp thesis: the three most important things that set someone apart in the AI age are Agency, Taste, and Distribution. The brief post drew 227 likes, capturing a widely felt question about which skills stay scarce as AI advances: when the barrier to execution gets flattened, the willingness to act, the judgment to choose well, and the ability to reach an audience become the new moat.
items.insightZh: Follow Builders 项目作者 Zara Zhang 给出了一个精炼的判断：在 AI 时代，真正让一个人脱颖而出的三件最重要的事是——Agency（主观能动性/行动力）、Taste（品味/判断力）、Distribution（分发/触达能力）。这条简短的观点收获了 227 个赞，戳中了很多人对「AI 时代什么能力最稀缺」的思考：当执行门槛被技术拉平后，敢做、会选、能传播，成了新的护城河。

items.title: How we contain Claude across products
items.summaryEn: Anthropic's engineering team published a candid, systematic account of how they contain Claude—prioritizing environment-layer defenses (sandboxes, VMs, egress controls) over model-layer and human approval alone. Twelve months ago Anthropic would have rejected granting Claude enough access to take down an internal service; today that's routine. They frame risk as two parts: how likely a failure is, and the "blast radius" if it happens. Telemetry showed users approve roughly 93% of permission prompts—the more they see, the less they scrutinize—so human-in-the-loop is fallible (auto mode cut prompts by 84%). The post lays out three isolation patterns: ephemeral gVisor containers for claude.ai, a human-in-the-loop sandbox for Claude Code (whose users can read bash), and a local VM for Claude Cowork (credentials stay in the host keychain). They own up to real incidents: a phished employee wh…
items.insightZh: 核心要点：Anthropic 工程团队系统性公开了他们如何「围堵」Claude——把安全防线优先放在环境层（沙箱、虚拟机、出口管控）而非只靠模型层和人工审批，并坦诚复盘了几次真实的安全翻车。 一年前 Anthropic 还会断然拒绝「给 Claude 足以搞垮内部服务的权限」这种想法，今天这种权限已成常态，开发者效率因此提升。文章把风险拆成两块：失败的概率，和一旦失败的「爆炸半径」。模型训练和防护手段不断压低前者，但后者只会随能力和权限扩张而增大。一个关键数据：他们的遥测显示用户对权限弹窗的批准率高达约 93%——看得越多越麻木，人工审批因此并不可靠（auto mode 让权限弹窗减少了 84%）。 文章给出三种隔离范式对应三款产品：claude.ai 用临时容器（gVisor，服务端，文件系统每会话即焚）；Claude Code 用「人在环路」沙箱（用户多是开发者，看得懂 bash）；Claude Cowork 用本地完整虚拟机（面向非技术知识工作者，凭据留在宿主钥匙串、永不进入虚拟机）。他们坦白了几次真实事故：钓鱼邮件诱导员工运行恶意 prompt，让 Claude 25 次里有 24 次把 AWS 凭据外传；以及通过「已批准域名」api.anthropic.com 用攻击者的 API key 把文件上传到攻击者账户——「沙箱完美工作，数据却照样被外传」。
